title: Range Rover L460
verdict: The most capable limousine ever to ask you to install a software update before breakfast. It will still crawl in low range — just don't expect the aftermarket, or the DC-DC converter, to keep up.
codes: I6 MHEV · BMW V8 · PHEV · EV

paragraphs: On 26 October 2021, Gerry McGovern pulled the covers off the fifth Range Rover at the Royal Opera House in London — a suitably theatrical venue for a truck that is mostly about refinement. The L460 keeps the family silhouette and the two-speed transfer box, then piles on things no Range Rover has had before: a seven-seat option, four-wheel steering, plug-in hybrids with a real electric range, a BMW-sourced V8 and, from the 2027 model year in America, a fully electric version. It is the most technically ambitious Range Rover yet, and its first few years brought a long list of recalls to match.

story.heading: MLA-FLEX AND THE BIG STRETCH
paragraphs: The L460 rides on JLR's MLA-Flex architecture, shared with the third-generation Range Rover Sport. It grew in every direction over the [[range-rover/l405|L405]]: 53 mm longer, 63 mm wider and 35 mm taller, on a wheelbase 75 mm longer at 2,997 mm. The long-wheelbase version adds another 200 mm between the axles, and it is the only body that offers seven seats. JLR claims torsional rigidity is up 50 percent to 50,000 Nm per degree, and a steel closed-section front bulkhead cuts road noise entering the cabin by about 24 percent.

Off-road hardware survived the luxury push. US-spec trucks still list a twin-speed transfer box with high and low range, Terrain Response 2, All Terrain Progress Control and hill descent control. Upper trims get an Electronic Active Differential with torque vectoring, while the SE makes do with an open rear diff and torque vectoring by braking. New tricks include all-wheel steering, the first on a Land Rover, which gives a 10.95 m turning circle. An intelligent AWD system can also disconnect the front axle between 35 and 160 km/h to cut drag losses by 30 percent.

story.heading: SIX, EIGHT, PLUG, BATTERY
paragraphs: Engines are all electrified to some degree. The core is JLR's 3.0-litre Ingenium straight-six, as a 400 PS mild-hybrid petrol, as 249–350 PS mild-hybrid diesels outside the US, or as a plug-in hybrid with a 38.2 kWh battery and a 105 kW motor (160 kW on the later P550e). The P440e and P510e launched the PHEVs, and the P550e replaced the P440e for the 2024 model year. The V8 is BMW's twin-turbo 4.4. Early P530s used the N63, and from the 2024 model year JLR switched to the newer S68, which also powers the 615 PS SV. In EPA testing a 2023 P530 managed 16 mpg city and 21 highway, the P400 18 and 26, and the P440e 51 MPGe on electricity.

Then the big one. Range Rover Electric is available to order in the US as a 2027 model, with twin 260 kW motors, 660 lb-ft, an 800-volt battery architecture and an EPA range of 333 miles. Land Rover is careful to say it is still a Range Rover. It quotes a 35-inch wading depth and 5,511 lb of towing, and the battery sits behind a flat, re-engineered underbody meant to cope with sliding over obstacles.

story.heading: GROWING PAINS
paragraphs: The launch was rough. Owners on FullFatRR report early cars delivered with downgraded audio and other options because JLR couldn't get the parts. Then came the recalls. NHTSA lists, among others, a blocked cam-carrier oil channel (2022–2023 L460s; the same campaign covers 2020–21 L405s), badly welded second-row seat frames on 2022–2023 seven-seaters, damaged tail-light links, and 2024 trucks with body panels that may not have been bonded properly. UK owners also reported a rear-subframe cracking recall in 2023. The headline problem now is the 48-volt to 12-volt DC-DC converter on mild hybrids: when it fails, the 12-volt battery stops charging. NHTSA recall 26V248000 covers 2020–2024 Range Rovers (including late L405 mild hybrids) with an interim central-software fix, and follow-up campaign 26V599000 adds a further software update, with a final remedy still to come.

None of that changes what it is on a trail: a very wide, very heavy luxury car with low range, clever traction electronics and air suspension that does its job well. What it lacks is an aftermarket. A 2025 FullFatRR thread asking for sliders and underbody protection was told to budget €3,500–4,000 for a fabrication shop. Owners weighing one for African dirt roads were pointed at a [[land-rover/defender-l663|Defender]] or a [[land-cruiser/300-series|Land Cruiser 300]]. Treat the L460 as a superb gravel-and-green-lane machine, and keep it away from rock gardens.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · RANGE ROVER ELECTRIC
callout.title: From −40 °F to the Arabian Desert
paragraphs: Before putting the electric L460 on sale, Land Rover ran it through what it calls one of its most arduous testing programmes. Product engineering director Thomas Müller took it into −40 °F conditions in the Arctic Circle, and test driver Yakub Dino drove it into the heat of the Arabian Desert.

The result: 344 nickel-manganese-cobalt cells stacked in two layers under a flat underbody, twin in-house 260 kW motors, a 35-inch wading depth, and single-pedal driving that works with Terrain Response to bring the truck to a stop on any surface. It's a 333-mile EPA-rated Range Rover that can still wade a ford. Spen King would probably want to know where the V8 went.

engineering_intro: The L460 is a mixed-material monocoque on JLR's MLA-Flex platform, built for electrification from the start: mild-hybrid, plug-in and battery-electric versions share the same body. It keeps the Range Rover essentials, with air suspension, permanent AWD and a two-speed transfer case on combustion models, then adds rear-wheel steering, a disconnecting front axle and a lot of software. For a hands-on owner, that means fewer bolt-on problems and more electrical ones. A capable scan tool is no longer optional.

engineering.note: Claimed 50,000 Nm/deg torsional rigidity (+50%); steel closed-section front bulkhead.
First Land Rover with it; 10.95 m turning circle (SWB), 11.54 m (LWB).
Twin-valve monotube dampers managed by Adaptive Dynamics; variable ride height.
Front axle can disconnect at 35–160 km/h; high and low range on combustion models.
With torque vectoring on upper trims; SE has an open rear diff with torque vectoring by braking (US spec).
3.0 Ingenium I6, BMW 4.4 V8 (N63 then S68), 38.2 kWh PHEV, 800 V Electric.

buying_checks.head: Run the VIN against every recall
buying_checks.body: NHTSA lists a stack of campaigns: a cam-carrier oil channel (2022–2023), 7-seat second-row frame welds (2022–2023), tail-light links (2022–2023), rear-camera water ingress (2022–2023) and tailgate camera drain holes (2022–2026), body panels not bonded properly (2024), transmission oil pressure (2024), a cracking oil filter housing (2024), the driver's airbag clockspring connector (2022–2026), and the DC-DC converter (26V248000 and 26V599000, 2022–2024 L460s). Get written confirmation that they're closed.

buying_checks.head: Ask about the DC-DC converter
buying_checks.body: On mild hybrids, a failing 48-volt to 12-volt converter shows 'Stop – electrical fault' with a red battery light and stops charging the 12-volt battery. Owners say it may log no fault and clear itself, only to return. Dealers have had cars waiting weeks for back-ordered modules. NHTSA recalls 26V248000 and 26V599000 are interim software updates, with a final remedy to follow.

buying_checks.head: Check that it goes to sleep
buying_checks.body: Flat 12-volt batteries after a few days parked are a recurring forum topic. Dealers have fixed some with door-module and other software updates, and one owner traced the same symptom to a brake-pedal security lock that kept the car from sleeping. Ask whether it has needed jump-starts, and whether any aftermarket immobiliser or tracker is fitted.

buying_checks.head: Check the build spec on early trucks
buying_checks.body: Owners say many early (2022) trucks were delivered with downgraded audio and other options during the parts shortage. Check the car against its original order or a parts catalogue before paying for options it doesn't have.

buying_checks.head: Know which V8 you're getting
buying_checks.body: P530s built for 2022–2023 use BMW's N63 twin-turbo V8, while 2024-on trucks got the newer S68. Forum owners rate the S68 as significantly more refined. It's also the engine in the SV P615.

buying_checks.head: Look at the service history, not just the stamps
buying_checks.body: Service intervals were up to 21,000 miles or 24 months, and owners report the 2024 model year D350 dropped to 10,500 miles or 12 months. Many owners change the oil more often than the schedule asks. A truck run to the maximum on short urban trips deserves extra scrutiny.

buying_checks.head: Check software and connectivity
buying_checks.body: Updates arrive over the air, but one 2022 owner whose truck was stuck on an old version found reports of a telematics (TCU) problem on some 2022–23 trucks. Check the software version against Land Rover's published releases, and confirm the remote app works.

buying_checks.head: Mind the wheel bolts and wheel size
buying_checks.body: The L460 uses wheel bolts, not the studs and nuts of the L405, so older Range Rover wheels need the correct flat-seat bolts. Owners say 22- and 23-inch wheels ride harshly on broken roads. For trail use, a smaller wheel with more sidewall is the better bet.

repairs.title: Rear brake pads (electric parking brake service mode)
repairs.symptoms: A pad-wear warning (one owner's P440e needed rear pads at 31,000 miles, another owner's at 16,000), or grinding at the rear. NHTSA has several similar complaints from 2023–24 owners, with pads worn out at roughly 10,000–17,000 miles; one 2023 long-wheelbase owner says the dealer blamed the design and fitted a different pad.
repairs.fix: The rear calipers use an electric parking brake, so put the brake into service (maintenance) mode before you push the pistons back. Shops do this with a scan tool. With the truck supported and the wheels off, remove the caliper, swap the pads (one owner fitted genuine pads and found a single wear sensor), refit, then take the brake out of service mode and check it applies properly.
repairs.tools: Jack and stands · sockets · pad spreader · scan tool with EPB service mode (e.g., GAP IID, which lists 2022–2025 L460 support) · new pads

parts.name: Bosch QuietCast rear brake pad set BP2464 (Range Rover 2022–25)

repairs.title: 12-volt battery replacement and BMS registration
repairs.cost: Auxiliary stop/start battery about $288 (Lucky8); parts plus labor
repairs.symptoms: 'Low battery, please start engine' messages, a truck that is electrically dead after a few days parked, or alarm and keyless-entry glitches.
repairs.fix: First rule out software (door-module and RFA updates have fixed some drains) and anything keeping the car awake. Then load-test the 12-volt battery. On a 2024 D350, one owner found the lithium-ion starter battery under the driver's seat, only removable with the truck on a ramp. A label under the bonnet says to jump-start at no more than 13.7 V, so don't use a random jump pack. Fit the correct battery type and register it with a diagnostic tool so the battery-management system charges it properly. Some trucks also carry an AGM auxiliary stop/start battery. Check fitment by VIN.
repairs.tools: Battery tester · lift or ramp (lithium battery under driver's seat on some trucks) · LR047630 / LR176847 auxiliary battery where fitted · diagnostic tool for BMS registration

parts.name: AGM auxiliary stop/start battery LR047630 / LR176847 (verify by VIN)

repairs.title: 48 V to 12 V DC-DC converter
repairs.cost: Specialist roughly £700–800 for the part plus about £400 to fit and program; dealers quoted £1,800–2,000 (owner reports)
repairs.symptoms: 'Stop – electrical fault detected' with a red battery light, the 12-volt battery not charging, and possibly loss of drive. Often no stored faults, and it may clear itself before coming back.
repairs.fix: Check first whether NHTSA recalls 26V248000 and 26V599000 (US) have been done. It adds a central software update to stop the converter overloading, and it's free. If the converter has already failed, it has to be replaced and then programmed to the vehicle, so use a dealer or a JLR specialist with the right software. Parts have been back-ordered, so plan on the truck being off the road for a while.
repairs.tools: JLR-capable diagnostic and programming tool · replacement DC-DC converter module

parts.name: L460 DC-DC converter (search; needs dealer programming)

repairs.title: Transfer box and driveline oil change
repairs.cost: Genuine fluid about £106 + VAT for 2 litres (owner report), plus labor
repairs.symptoms: Preventive. Owners suggest doing the transfer box at around 60,000 miles, along with the ZF gearbox and both differentials.
repairs.fix: Drain and refill the transfer box with about 2 litres of the fluid Land Rover specifies. Owners argue about cheaper alternatives, and one experienced member insists a generic transfer fluid is the wrong oil for the L460, so check the handbook rather than forum advice. One owner notes the front-axle disconnect clutch uses the same fluid as the active rear differential.
repairs.tools: Sockets and drain plugs/washers · fluid pump · Land Rover-specified transfer fluid (≈ 2 L)

repairs.title: Engine oil and filter (shorter interval)
repairs.symptoms: None. Owners just don't trust a 20,000-mile interval, and the 2024 model-year D350 schedule dropped to 10,500 miles or 12 months.
repairs.fix: Drain the sump, replace the cartridge filter and refill with the specified oil, then reset the service counter with a scan tool. Lubricate both sealing rings on the filter's neck, because a dry filter can twist on installation. Many owners on FullFatRR change oil well ahead of the onboard reminder.
repairs.tools: Sockets · filter housing tool · drain pan · new sump plug washer · correct-spec oil · scan tool for service reset (e.g., GAP IID)

parts.name: Genuine oil filter kit LR133455 (3.0 Ingenium I6, Range Rover 2020–25)
Oil filter LR133455 with O-ring (Lucky8 lists Ingenium 3.0 Defender/RR fitment — confirm L460 by VIN)

repairs.title: Factory-style tow hitch and wiring
repairs.cost: About $1,288 (genuine NAS hitch) to $1,628 (Lucky8 receiver + wiring combo)
repairs.symptoms: No receiver, and you have a 7,716 lb-rated truck and a trailer.
repairs.fix: Fit the receiver to the rear structure, run the towing harness, install the towing module (ECU) and fit the bumper trim finisher. The Lucky8 combo fits SWB trucks only, and the supplier needs the VIN because trucks with and without a third row, and different trim colours, take different parts.
repairs.tools: Sockets and torque wrench · trim tools · Lucky8 RRL460TOWKITVINFIRST combo or genuine VPLKT0326 hitch · towing module VPLYT0295

parts.name: Genuine Range Rover L460 trailer hitch kit (NAS)
Towing receiver + complete wiring combo, L460 (SWB)

repairs.title: Cracked oil filter housing
repairs.cost: Free under recall 24V-450 (Land Rover N908); otherwise parts plus labor
repairs.symptoms: Oil seeping around the oil filter housing, a hot-oil smell from the engine bay, or the oil level dropping between services. Land Rover recalled certain 2024 Range Rovers, plus some 2023–24 Defenders and 2024 Discoverys, Range Rover Sports and Velars, because the housing can crack and leak oil into the engine compartment, where it can catch fire on hot engine or exhaust parts.
repairs.fix: Run the VIN first. The recall remedy is a new filter housing, oil filter and O-rings, fitted free by a dealer (owner letters went out in June 2024). On a truck outside the recall that's leaking from the same place, the repair is the same: replace the housing with new O-rings and a new filter, following the workshop procedure for your engine, top up the oil and check for leaks at temperature. Clean any oil off the exhaust and undertrays afterwards.
repairs.tools: Sockets and torque wrench · drain pan · new O-rings lubricated with clean oil · brake cleaner and rags

parts.name: Genuine oil filter kit LR133455 (3.0 Ingenium I6, Range Rover 2020–25)

repairs.title: Rear camera water damage
repairs.cost: Free under recalls 24V-947 and 26V-678; otherwise a camera plus labor
repairs.symptoms: A blank, fogged or distorted rear-view image, or a camera fault message when you select reverse. Land Rover has recalled the L460's rear camera twice for water: 2022–23 trucks because water can get inside the camera (24V-947), and 2022–26 trucks because there aren't enough drain holes for water to escape the camera area (26V-678).
repairs.fix: Run the VIN. Under 24V-947 dealers replace the camera; under 26V-678 they drill extra drain holes in the underside of the tailgate trim and replace the camera if it's damaged. Land Rover planned to mail interim owner letters for 26V-678 in December 2026. On a truck you wash often or take through water crossings, keep the area under the tailgate trim clear of mud so water can drain.
repairs.tools: Trim-removal tools · scan tool to calibrate the surround cameras after a camera change (dealer or JLR specialist)

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: There is no forum consensus yet. Owners haven't published L460 all-terrain fitment the way L405 owners have, and the off-the-shelf sensor-link lift kits sold for the L405 don't list the L460. Factory wheels run from 20 to 23 inches, and one owner fitted L460 21s with 275/50R21 tyres to an L405. If you want sidewall, 20-inch wheels are the realistic floor: Lucky8 lists 20×9.5 ET30 wheels for the L460, and L405 20s fit with the correct flat-seat bolts. Test any oversize tyre at full lock and in every height mode before you trust it.

faq.q: What fuel economy should I expect?
faq.a: For 2023, the EPA rated the P400 at 18 mpg city, 26 highway and 21 combined, and the 4.4 V8 at 16/21/18. The P440e plug-in hybrid was rated 51 MPGe on electricity and 21 mpg on petrol alone.

Land Rover USA quotes up to 7,716 lb for the P400 and the V8s, 6,614 lb for the current plug-in hybrid, and 5,511 lb for Range Rover Electric. Earlier P440e trucks were listed at 5,511 lb. Check the figure for your exact model year and powertrain.

faq.q: Does it still have low range and a locking diff?
faq.a: Combustion and hybrid models keep a twin-speed transfer box with high and low range. Upper trims get an Electronic Active Differential with torque vectoring, while the base SE has an open rear differential with torque vectoring by braking. Terrain Response 2, All Terrain Progress Control and hill descent control are standard.

2022–2023 P530s use BMW's N63 twin-turbo 4.4. From the 2024 model year, JLR fitted BMW's S68, also used in the 615 PS SV. Owners on FullFatRR call the S68 'significantly more refined.' It's too early for long-term reliability data on either in this truck.

faq.q: How far does the plug-in hybrid go on electricity?
faq.a: PHEVs use a 38.2 kWh battery (31.8 kWh usable) with a 105 kW motor on the P440e/P510e and a 160 kW motor on the P550e. Land Rover estimates about 50 miles of real-world electric range. A 7 kW home charger fills it in about 5 hours, and a 50 kW DC charger gets it to 80% in under an hour.

Yes. Range Rover Electric is on order books in the US for the 2027 model year. It has an EPA-estimated range of 333 miles, twin 260 kW motors, 660 lb-ft, 800 V charging (10–80% in about 22 minutes on a 350 kW charger), a 35-inch wading depth and 5,511 lb of towing.

Only in the long-wheelbase body, and Land Rover USA says LWB seven-seaters aren't available as plug-in hybrids or EVs. Four- and five-seat layouts are also offered. Check recall 23V252000 on 2022–2023 seven-seaters for the second-row seat frame welds.

The early record is mixed. NHTSA lists more than a dozen recalls across the 2023 and 2024 model years, and the DC-DC converter, 12-volt battery drain and software glitches dominate the FullFatRR technical board. Buy one with a warranty, a clean recall record and connected software that actually updates.

faq.q: Which years are the best to buy?
faq.a: Too early to call. NHTSA lists ten or eleven recalls for each of the 2022, 2023 and 2024 model years, so later trucks aren't clean either: 2022–23 carry the cam-carrier, seat-frame and tail-light campaigns, and 2024 adds panel-bonding, transmission and oil-filter-housing recalls. Owners prefer the 2024-on S68 V8. Buy on a closed recall list, a warranty and software that actually updates, not on the model year.

faq.q: Can I use a GAP tool on it?
faq.a: Yes. GAP's IID G4 lists 2022–2025 L460s on the standard tool, for fault codes, live data, service resets, calibrations, air-suspension height adjustment and CCF edits. FullFatRR owners use it for proximity-locking and other CCF tweaks.

faq.q: Can I get sliders or a bash plate?
faq.a: Not easily. A 2025 FullFatRR thread found no off-the-shelf sliders or underbody protection, and members suggested a fabrication shop would charge €3,500–4,000 for tree sliders and plates. It's a gap the aftermarket hasn't filled the way it has for the L405.

mods.why: Smaller rims mean more sidewall for gravel and green lanes than the factory 22s and 23s, and more choice of all-terrain tyres. Lucky8 lists these 20×9.5 ET30 wheels for the L460.
Dealer-level diagnostics at home: EPB service mode, BMS registration, air-suspension heights and calibration, and configuration edits.
The L460's electrics are hungry. Keep the right replacement and charging kit on hand rather than a random jump pack.

Genuine fixed-point cross bars bolt to four discreet mounting points in the roof, so no roof rails are needed. LR Parts lists them at a 100 kg maximum carrying capacity. Check the vehicle's own roof-load limit too.

baseline_service.intro: The L460 is new enough that most trucks will have dealer history. Still, the first job is the recall and software status, because several known faults (DC-DC converter, battery drain) are fixed by updates. Fluid specs differ by powertrain (Ingenium I6 diesel or petrol, BMW V8, PHEV) and the BorgWarner transfer box takes its own fluid, so read the owner's handbook for your VIN rather than reusing L405 figures.

items.note: Recalls 26V248000 and 26V599000 (US) add central software updates so the 48 V–12 V converter doesn't overload, and door-module and RFA updates have cured some battery drains. All are free and stop expensive failures.

items.item: Front axle disconnect & active rear differential
items.spec: One owner reports the front-axle disconnect clutch uses the same fluid as the Electronic Active Differential · [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
items.note: SE trims in the US may have an open rear diff with brake-based torque vectoring, so check which you have before ordering fluid.

items.spec: Pads, rotors and brake fluid · fluid [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
items.interval: Inspect at purchase. Owners have needed rear pads at 16,000–31,000 mi
items.note: The rear calipers have an electric parking brake, so put them in service mode with a scan tool before you push the pistons back.

parts.name: Bosch QuietCast rear pads BP2464 (Range Rover 2022–25)
Bosch QuietCast front pads BP2463 (Range Rover 2022–25)

items.spec: Lithium-ion starter battery on some trucks (under the driver's seat on a 2024 D350), plus an AGM auxiliary battery on stop/start trucks
items.note: A bonnet label says to jump-start at no more than 13.7 V. Register any new battery with a scan tool.

parts.name: AGM auxiliary stop/start battery LR047630 / LR176847 (verify by VIN)

items.note: There's a FullFatRR thread on cracking L460 subframes, so inspect them on a lift, along with the air springs and their lines.
